# RETRO: #12999 follow-up (team 1)

## What worked
- One neutral brief for both reviewers; both finals were independent.
- The Opus sealed fixture covered the upgrade eras thoroughly.
- A single neutral follow-up to Sol on fontconfig precedence resolved the severity disagreement without quoting the peer.

## Process deviations (candid)
- **Incidental exposure:** the `pi_job.py wait` output receipt includes Sol's `latest_text`, so the coordinator saw Sol's closing headline before the Opus final existed. It was not disclosed to Opus, and the Opus brief and prompt were already fixed. Suggested tooling change: make `wait` print lifecycle fields only.
- **Archive members:** the coordinator extracted `git archive` output of the pinned commits without first listing members. The source was GitHub commits fetched by SHA, and the extraction was read-only afterwards. Recorded; the next round should list members first.
- **Host conf.d read:** the Opus fixture used a private copy of the sandbox-visible host `/etc/fonts/conf.d` (read only, no writes). This is disclosed in REPORT limits; the public claims are scoped to substitution order.
- **Blobless upstream clones:** each reviewer made its own under its output directory (read-only research, as the brief allowed).

## Carry forward
- The `pi_job.py wait` output should omit reviewer prose.
- Note in the brief that the shallow pinned repo lacks history; reviewers fetched history themselves.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up at head `e239256` to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12999#issuecomment-5791068152) and the [author's update](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12999#issuecomment-5799195505). The earlier finding is resolved. One smaller issue remains: the new cleanup fails silently.

### Earlier finding: resolved

**Verified:** "Migrate the previously generated monospace rule" is resolved. When a new font is selected, the setter removes the `prepend_first` rule that earlier v4 setters wrote to `~/.config/fontconfig/fonts.conf`, keeps other user rules in that file, and the new drop-in wins. Older 3.x-style rules (`assign`/`append`) are left untouched and do not override the drop-in. The results below come from a fontconfig 2.18.3 substitution check run against the real setters with synthetic families:

| `fonts.conf` before selecting B | Setter | `fonts.conf` after | First family |
|---|---|---|---|
| Earlier generated rule for A | `60f9335` | unchanged | A |
| Earlier generated rule for A | `e239256` | removed | B |
| Earlier generated rule for A, plus an unrelated user rule | `e239256` | only the generated block removed | B |
| 3.x-style `assign` rule for A | `e239256` | byte-identical | B |
| Earlier generated rule for A, file read-only | `e239256` | unchanged, exit 0, no output | **A** |

A and B are synthetic family names. The check covers substitution order, not rendered fonts.

### Cleanup failures are silent

The last table row shows the problem. At [`bin/omarchy-font-set:98-99`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/e239256104278b26d1c26e20badfa37fcf4e1126/bin/omarchy-font-set#L98-L99), `except Exception: pass` discards every read, decode and write error. The setter then restarts the shell and exits 0. In the other direction, the result of writing the drop-in at [line 59](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/e239256104278b26d1c26e20badfa37fcf4e1126/bin/omarchy-font-set#L59) is not checked before the cleanup runs. If that write fails, the old rule can be removed while the new one is never written. The read-only case above was executed; the unchecked drop-in write is identified from source.

The cleanup is also silent when it succeeds. It removes every block with the generated shape, including a user-written rule of that shape (seen in the synthetic check) and markup inside XML comments (source only). It can also delete the whole file. Removing an active rule of that shape is consistent with selecting a new font, because such a rule would otherwise override the selection. Nothing tells the user a change was made, though.

**Impact:** when the rewrite fails, the earlier symptom returns with no hint: fontconfig consumers keep the old family while terminal configuration changes to the new one.

**Suggested change:** run the cleanup only after the drop-in write succeeds. Report a cleanup failure, naming `~/.config/fontconfig/fonts.conf`, instead of passing silently. Print a short message when a rule or the file is removed. Optionally, skip commented-out markup.

**Documentation note:** the comment at [`shell/Commons/Style.qml:460-462`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/e239256104278b26d1c26e20badfa37fcf4e1126/shell/Commons/Style.qml#L460-L462) still says the setter rewrites `~/.config/fontconfig/fonts.conf`.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** head `e239256`, compared with `60f9335`. Source inspection of the setter, the shell watcher, earlier setter generations and fontconfig's load-order and `prepend_first` source. Native fontconfig 2.18.3 substitution checks ran the real setters in an isolated environment with synthetic families and stubbed desktop commands. Not covered: installed-font matching, the shell, terminals, the GUI, and a live upgrade.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis; independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments of this revision, with a targeted follow-up question; Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
